control: CURRENT-VINTAGE PUBLIC RULES LAYER -- NYSRC Reliability Rules & Compliance Manual V48 (final, 7-17-2026), Section G 'Local Area Operation'
purpose: The first real application of the nyiso-163 gate. These are the CURRENT-vintage successors of the 2008 Table B.4 Con Edison in-City rows, transcribed from a PUBLIC source. Running the gate on them tests whether the public rules layer identifies the in-City commitment formation at 2023-2025 vintage.
scope_warning: THIS IS NOT THE ARTIFACT INTAKE-SPEC-nyiso156 §2 ASKS FOR. The spec asks for the Applications of the Reliability Rules (AORR / former Manual 12 Table B.5), which remain at a login-walled NYISO location. This fixture is the RULES layer; the Applications are the PROCEDURES layer that implements it. A FAIL here therefore re-confirms nyiso-97 at current vintage but does NOT discharge Leg 2 -- only the walled Applications table can do that.
provenance: Fetched and transcribed 2026-08-31 (nyiso-163) from https://www.nysrc.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/RRC-Manual-V48-final-7-17-2026.pdf, linked from https://www.nysrc.org/documents/nysrc-reliability-rules-compliance-monitoring/ . Routing verified in the CURRENT NYISO Manual 12 (issued July 2026, https://www.nyiso.com/documents/20142/2923301/trans_disp.pdf), whose Attachment B replaces the former Appendix B tables with links: Table B.4 -> the NYSRC Reliability Rules (public), Table B.5 / ARR -> https://www.nyiso.com/reports-information (login-walled).
transcription_note: Text is verbatim from the source with whitespace normalised only. Each row is encoded as generously as the published text honestly allows.

rows.row_id: NYSRC RR V48 G.1 R1 (Con Edison second contingency) -- successor of Table B.4 LRR 1
rows.source: NYSRC Reliability Rules & Compliance Manual V48, 7-17-2026, G.1 New York City System Operations, B. Requirements R1
rows.text: Certain areas of the Con Edison system shall be designed and operated for the occurrence of a second contingency.
rows.note: Materially unchanged from the 2008 LRR 1 wording. Still qualitative: no MW level, no unit set, no observable trigger.
rows.vintage_basis: v46 (2022-06-10) in force at span start; no Section-G requirement revised at v47 or v48; last Section-G change v42 (2018-02-09).

rows.row_id: NYSRC RR V48 G.1 R2 (NYC zone unit commitment) -- successor of Table B.4 LRR 1 commitment sentence
rows.source: NYSRC Reliability Rules & Compliance Manual V48, 7-17-2026, G.1, B. Requirements R2
rows.text: Unit commitment in the New York City (NYC) zone shall be based on second contingency operation and consideration of the Storm Watch Procedure, loss of the six lines south of Millwood, and the locational requirements for operating reserves.
rows.note: THIS is the row the winter face would need. It is the direct current-vintage statement of the in-City commitment obligation -- and it states no MW level, no minimum-units count, no eligible unit set and no observable trigger. It defers entirely to procedures.
rows.vintage_basis: v46 (2022-06-10) in force at span start; no Section-G requirement revised at v47 or v48; last Section-G change v42 (2018-02-09).

rows.row_id: NYSRC RR V48 G.1 R3.2 (NYC locational 10-minute reserve share)
rows.source: NYSRC Reliability Rules & Compliance Manual V48, 7-17-2026, G.1, B. Requirements R3.2
rows.text: A percentage of the ten (10) minute NYCA operating reserves equal to the ratio of the NYC zone peak load to the statewide peak load shall be required to be selected from resources located within the NYC zone.

units: resources located within the NYC zone
eligible_unit_set.quote: resources located within the NYC zone

rows.note: THE CLOSEST ROW TO IDENTIFYING in the entire public layer, and the one place the gate's verbatim-number requirement does real work. The row states a DERIVATION RULE (share = NYC peak / statewide peak) rather than a level: no MW number appears in the text, and the NYCA 10-minute reserve it scales is set by a different rule. It is also a LOCATIONAL RESERVE requirement, not the in-City COMMITMENT formation the winter face needs -- arming it would be a reserve lever, which rule 19 [R-ONE-MECH] and the ledgered-C3c queue closure forbid. Flagged for the owner rather than silently adjudicated; see the nyiso-163 finding §4.
rows.vintage_basis: v46 (2022-06-10) in force at span start; no Section-G requirement revised at v47 or v48; last Section-G change v42 (2018-02-09).

rows.row_id: NYSRC RR V48 G.2 R3 (published MOB dual-fuel unit list)
rows.source: NYSRC Reliability Rules & Compliance Manual V48, 7-17-2026, G.2 Loss of Gas Supply - New York City, B. Requirements R3
rows.pocket: New York City / Minimum Oil Burn program
rows.text: The NYISO shall document, maintain and publish the current list of dual fuel units that are part of the Minimum Oil Burn (MOB) program.
rows.note: Does not itself carry the unit set -- it obliges the NYISO to publish one elsewhere. That published MOB list is a concrete, separately-requestable artifact and is added to the access package as item (d). Note the settlement side of this rule (LRR I-R3 & I-R5, Min Oil Burn) is live in 2023-2025 per the NYISO Accounting & Billing Training Reference v1.0 (11/18/2024) bill codes 328/839 -- but that is a make-whole OUTCOME and is barred as a requirement substitute by rule 13 and the nyiso-97 §5 re-open bar.
rows.vintage_basis: v46 (2022-06-10) in force at span start; no Section-G requirement revised at v47 or v48; last Section-G change v42 (2018-02-09).

rows.row_id: NYSRC RR V48 G.2 D (Guidelines: where the MOB parameters actually live)
rows.source: NYSRC Reliability Rules & Compliance Manual V48, 7-17-2026, G.2, D. Guidelines
rows.text: There are applications, approved by the NYISO for implementing this Reliability Rule, which specify minimum oil burn requirements for select generators in New York City.
rows.note: THE DECISIVE ROW. The current public rules layer states in terms that the operative in-City parameters live in the APPLICATIONS, not in the rules. This is nyiso-97 §4 blocker 1 restated by the source itself at July-2026 vintage: the rule is public, the parameters are not. NYSRC §1.2.8 defines Applications as 'operating procedures that apply to very specific system locations or conditions' and routes them to https://www.nyiso.com/reliability-compliance ; Manual 12 Table B.5 routes the ARR table to https://www.nyiso.com/reports-information . Both are NYISO-side; nyiso-97 established the latter is MyNYISO-walled.
rows.vintage_basis: v46 (2022-06-10) in force at span start; no Section-G requirement revised at v47 or v48; last Section-G change v42 (2018-02-09).

vintage_evidence: IN FORCE UNCHANGED ACROSS 2023-2025, established from the manual's own Version History (V48 section 8): v46 (6/10/2022) was in force at 2023-01-01; v47 (6/14/2024) changed only RR B.5 / B.1 / Tables B-1 and B-3; v48 (6/17/2026) changed only RR A.2. The last revision to ANY Section-G requirement was v42 (2/9/2018, G.2 R1/R2 and G.3 R1/R2 per PRR 138/139). Therefore the G.1 and G.2 text quoted here from V48 is the text that was in force for the whole of the 2023-2025 scored span. Rows are encoded with vintage_effective_start = 2022-06-10 (the v46 issue date, in force at span start) rather than the V48 edition date, which would conflate edition with effectivity. This is what INTAKE-SPEC-nyiso156 §2 item (c) asks a current snapshot to establish, and it is established here from the source's own change history.
